messages:
Alex K: Heads-up — we got a flurry of pagers for embeddings latency across us-east-1 around 09:04. Paging spam from the same alert group; looks like noisy signal rather than several independent failures. @Maya R are you oncall now?
Maya R: oncall here. I saw the incidentbot stream. Looking at traces now, tail latency spikes line up with a sudden increase in long queries from an internal crawler job. Not customer-facing yet, but some customers saw slow embed writes.
Samir: +1 saw a small uptick in 5xxs on the embeddings write path in the last 10m (ALB error rate). Collecting logs.
IncidentBot: [ALERT] embeddings.latency.high triggered 6x in 5m (channel: eng-oncall)
Jin Park: FYI @Alex K tagging the customer-impact flow. Should we temporarily squelch duplicate paging and add an alert grouping window? Paging is drowning the rotation.
Alex K: Yes — we need to avoid pagerstorm. Plan: 1) mute noisy duplicate alerts (squelch) 2) update alert thresholds and grouping in Datadog 3) add a short dashboard and runbook note so next oncall can see mitigation steps. Any objections?
Maya R: agree. I'll take ownership for the immediate mitigation (squelch & grouping). Samir can you confirm whether we should page on rate or only on sustained p50/p95 above Xms?
Samir: running a quick query — looks like 95th jumps >1s for ~2–3 minutes during bursts but median unaffected. I think change to: only page when p95 > 800ms for >= 5m AND write error rate > 0.5%. That should drop the noise.
Alex K: sounds good. Put that as the new threshold and leave a note in the runbook. Also add a link to the new dashboard with the burst query.
Maya R: performing squelch on the alert group now (5m). Also creating a short dashboard named "embeddings/latency-burst" with charts for p50/p95, write errors, and top 10 callers by token_count.
Maya R: patched alert to:
```
query: p95(latency) > 0.8s AND sum(write_errors) / sum(requests) > 0.005 over 5m
notify: pager (prod-oncall)
group_by: service, region
```
Maya R: applied, testing. Will leave paging enabled for sustained issues only.
Samir: logs show internal job id crawler-129 spiking calls with huge batch sizes — created a temporary rate-limit on that caller at the gateway to avoid cascading.
Jin Park: nice. Please add the gateway rate-limit rule in the runbook so it's discoverable. Link to rule: https://redwood.internal/gateway/rate-limits/crawler-129
Alex K: I'm updating the runbook entry (embeddings runbook) with the following items: mitigation steps, who to notify for customer-impact (SE rotation), and links to the dashboard and gateway rule. I'll put a clear annotation: "temporary squelch applied — revert after follow-up". Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-latency
Alex K: runbook changes (summary):
- Owner: @Maya R
- Pager condition updated (p95 + error rate)
- Squelch procedure documented (how to apply/remove)
- Dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/embeddings-latency-burst
- Gateway rule link: https://redwood.internal/gateway/rate-limits/crawler-129
Maya R: updated the runbook section and added an annotations section: `annotation: 1797654321 - squelch applied, threshold tightened, gateway rule added, follow-up: investigate crawler batch sizing`
IncidentBot: Incident resolved: duplicates suppressed; alert frequency reduced.
Samir: leaving a quick post-incident note: root cause seems to be a new job rollout that increased batch size by 10x. I opened an internal ticket for the job owner: JOB-4521.
Alex K: thanks. Action items before handoff:
1) Samir to own postmortem and JOB-4521 follow-up (owner: Samir)
2) Maya to keep the squelch in place and monitor for 3 hours; if steady, remove squelch and leave thresholds (owner: Maya R)
3) Alex to update runbook and notify SE rotation about customers touched (owner: Alex K)
4) Jin to propose a permanent alert grouping/aggregation policy for low-signal noisy alerts (owner: Jin Park)
Maya R: acknowledged. I'll monitor and post another update in ~2h. If anything escalates I'll page per the new rule.
Jin Park: I'll schedule a quick FYI doc in infra-weekly to propose the aggregation policy and examples.
Alex K: handoff to next oncall: @Samir will check in at 11:30 for follow-up; current oncall remains Maya until 10:30. Please reference the runbook link above during handoff.
Samir: will follow up. Leaving a short note for SEs: "Potential customer slowdowns observed — mitigated. If customers report degraded embed writes around 09:00-09:10, refer to runbook and JOB-4521."
Maya R: closing the immediate thread. Thanks team :thumbsup:
